reference: No GNU mouse CLI exists. Fixed records follow XTerm Control Sequences mouse tracking: X10 adds 32 to button/coordinates, 1015 adds 32 to the button only, and SGR carries the unoffset button and lowercase-m release. Modifiers are 4/8/16, motion 32 and vertical wheel 64/65. Stable record spelling follows the documented API. DEC mode-emission bytes follow the same published terminal protocol and are captured as ordinary stdout.
coverage: SGR press, drag, vertical wheel, modifiers and explicit release
1015 offset normalization for all three ordinary buttons, modifiers, motion, vertical wheel and release
1015 direct decimal coordinates beyond X10 limits and X10 unsigned byte coordinates
Valid hex word splitting and prefixes
Exact DEC mouse-mode output bytes captured without accessing a terminal.
exclusions: No external GNU mouse CLI exists; no GNU parity claimed.
Metadata and version banners are not operation coverage or GNU byte-equality tests.
Extended buttons, any-event hover semantics, UTF-8 1005, pixel 1016, streams and terminal lifecycle are outside these fixtures.
Mode-emission cases capture escape bytes as stdout only. Actual terminal negotiation, input devices and live mode changes remain deferred.

cases.purpose: Malformed terminators, decimal fields beyond the decoder's supported range, and odd-length hex are rejected with usage status instead of being emitted as events.
cases.script:
rc=0
mouse decode 1b5b3c303b313b315a || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 2 ]] || exit 20
rc=0
mouse decode 1b5b3c303b313030303030313b314d || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 2 ]] || exit 21
rc=0
mouse decode 1b5b3c0 || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 2 ]] || exit 22
printf 'invalid records rejected\n'

cases.purpose: In urxvt 1015, wire Cb=32 represents normalized button code 0 (button-1 press); the 32 protocol offset must not be mistaken for the SGR motion bit.
cases.stdout: mouse protocol=1015 kind=press button=button1 x=4 y=6 mods= code=0

cases.purpose: X10 encodes button and coordinates with a +32 offset; these vectors check the inverse transform plus shift and release interpretation.

mouse protocol=x10 kind=press button=button1 x=8 y=18 mods=shift code=4
mouse protocol=x10 kind=release button=release x=1 y=1 mods= code=3

cases.purpose: Ordinary invalid records reject button fields below the wire offset, lowercase-m releases (SGR only), missing separators, and trailing bytes; emit no event.
cases.script:
for record in 1b5b303b313b314d 1b5b33313b313b314d 1b5b33353b313b316d 1b5b33323b31314d 1b5b33323b313b314d00; do
  rc=0
  mouse decode "$record" || rc=$?
  [[ $rc == 2 ]] || exit 20
done
printf 'invalid 1015 records rejected\n'

cases.purpose: End-to-end terminal reporting and mode negotiation remain outside pure-byte decoding.
Bash reports mouse as a loadable builtin, which is the documented availability contract.
The Bash help builtin exposes the mouse description and its documented decode and mode forms.
cases.script:
h=$(help mouse)
[[ $h == *"Decode terminal mouse events and emit DEC mouse mode toggles."* ]] || exit 10
[[ $h == *"mouse decode HEX..."* ]] || exit 11
[[ $h == *"mouse enable [1006|1015|x10|all]"* ]] || exit 12
printf 'help metadata present\n'

cases.purpose: Selective mode commands emit the corresponding DEC private mode for SGR 1006, urxvt 1015, and legacy X10 mode 1000.
cases.script:
mouse enable 1006
mouse disable 1006
mouse enable 1015
mouse disable 1015
mouse enable x10
mouse disable x10

cases.purpose: The default enable mode and explicit all-mode disable emit all three supported DEC mode sequences in documented order.
Exercise enable/decode/disable against terminal input and verify mode cleanup across a bounded consumer lifecycle.
